title: Service Contracts → SLO Translation Workshop: Tactical Notes & Action Items
summary: Notes and tactical actions from a cross-functional workshop focused on converting external service contract commitments and internal service-level agreements into measurable SLOs and error budget policies.
background: We ran a 3-hour cross-functional session to close the gap between customer-facing contract language (uptime, response times, throughput guarantees) and operational signals we can measure. Attendees included SRE, platform, product, legal, and solutions engineering. The goal was to produce concrete SLO drafts, instrumentation requirements, and a 6-week cutover plan for two high-risk customer-facing areas.
workshop-goals: (1) Map contractual commitments to candidate SLOs with clear metrics and windows. (2) Define error budget consumption semantics and escalation policy. (3) List telemetry gaps and immediate instrumentation tasks. (4) Assign owners for rollout, testing, and customer communication.
agenda: Introductions (10m); Contract review & pain signals (30m); Metric mapping breakout (60m); SLO drafting and thresholds (40m); Instrumentation gaps & tickets (25m); Actions, owners, timeline (15m).
key-decisions: 1) Use 'request success rate' for availability SLOs rather than host-level pings to reflect user experience. 2) 30-day rolling window chosen for availability SLOs for production public API; 7-day window for fast-feedback internal endpoints. 3) Alerting: separate 'SLO burn' alerts (team-level) from immediate incident alerts (pager). 4) Contractual language offering "99.95% uptime" will be translated to a concrete SLO of 99.93% availability with defined allowed maintenance windows and documented measurement rules.
slo-proposals: Hosted API availability: metric = successful generation responses / total requests (filtering out client errors 4xx), target = 99.93%, window = 30d, burn thresholds = 3% of error budget in 1d (warning) and 10% in 1d (critical). Dedicated control-plane latency: metric = 95th percentile config-apply latency, target = <= 250ms, window = 14d, measurement = service-metrics:control_plane.apply_latency_p95. Private admin portal: metric = page load time (TTI), target = <= 1.2s p90, window = 7d (internal), lower-priority for contractual commitments but monitored for regressions.
measurement-specs: Define exact Prometheus queries and synthetic checks for each SLO. Example for Hosted API availability: (sum(rate(api_responses_total{code!~\"4..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(api_requests_total[5m]))) aggregated to daily and computed as 30-day rolling availability. Synthetic canary: 5 synthetic user flows from three regions every 5 minutes.
instrumentation-actions:
- Add response-status label to api_requests_total and api_responses_total (owner: Kai, due: 2026-09-14)
- Create synthetic flows in canary runner and record results to synthetic_checks_up (owner: Priya, due: 2026-09-18)
- Add control-plane.apply_latency_p95 metric (owner: Miguel, due: 2026-09-16)
- Document filtering rules for client errors and maintenance windows in Confluence (owner: Evelyn, due: 2026-09-20)
escalation-and-burn-policy:
- Warning alert when 3% of monthly error budget consumed in any 24h window: notify on-call Slack + SLO channel.
- Critical alert when 10% consumed in 24h: page SRE primary and product lead.
- If >50% budget consumed in 7d: open incident bridge and execute mitigation playbook (fallback models, route to lower-cost region).
risks-and-unknowns: 1) Telemetry gaps on long-tail failure modes (e.g., partial token truncation) may undercount user-impacting errors. 2) Contractual definitions of 'downtime' differ by region; need legal sign-off on measurement rules. 3) Synthetic checks might not capture real workload patterns for embeddings heavy customers.
communications-plan: Customer-facing: Draft a short note for customers affected by SLO definition changes explaining measurement method and any impact on SLA enforcement (owner: Jordan, due: 2026-09-24). Internal: Weekly SRE synched status update and a short product-ops review before rollout.
rollout-timeline: Week 0 (2026-09-07): finalize SLO language and instrumentation tickets. Week 1: implement metrics and synthetic checks. Week 2: run parallel SLO computation using new metrics for 7 days (shadow mode). Week 3: review shadow results and adjust. Week 4: switch SLO to production and enable SLO burn alerts. Week 6: customer comms and SLA alignment meeting.

success-criteria:
- Full SLO computation runs in <2h for 30-day window and matches shadow within 0.02% discrepancy.
- Synthetic checks correlate with at least 80% of observed real-user error spikes over the shadow week.
- Legal signs off on measurement rules and maintenance window semantics.
- Customers on Dedicated tier with contractual uptime guarantees have clear doc mapping to the defined SLOs.
follow-ups-and-next-meeting: Weekly check-ins (30m) on Fridays at 09:30 starting 2026-09-11 until rollout complete. Next deep-review scheduled 2026-09-21 to evaluate shadow run outputs.
notes-to-self: Keep SLA math conservative when mapping to contract penalties. Prioritize clarity of measurement over aggressive targets. If telemetry gaps persist, use synthetic checks as a stop-gap while engineering fills metric gaps.
